title: Controlling Silica Dust Exposure
summary: Cutting, grinding, and jackhammering concrete, brick, mortar, and rock release crystalline silica dust that causes silicosis, lung cancer, COPD, and kidney disease. This talk covers water, vacuums, and respiratory protection.
talking_points: Use water or vacuum dust collection to control dust at the source before it becomes airborne. When that is not enough, add respiratory protection.
Keep dust control systems working. Check vacuum filters and hoses often so they do not clog.
Do not use sand or other material with more than 1% crystalline silica for abrasive blasting. Substitute a less hazardous material.
If a safer material is not available, use the correct respiratory protection.
Do not eat, drink, or smoke in dusty areas. Leave the area and wash your hands and face first.
Do not carry dust home. Vacuum your clothes or change into clean clothes before you leave. Never brush or blow dust off.
site_hazards_to_check: Dry cutting, grinding, or drilling of concrete, masonry, or stone with no water or vacuum
Clogged or damaged vacuum filters and hoses, or empty water tanks
Sand or high-silica media used for abrasive blasting
Visible dust clouds drifting toward other workers nearby
Workers brushing or blowing dust off clothing
discussion_questions: What silica-generating tasks are happening today, and what dust controls are set up?
Who nearby could be exposed to dust that drifts from your task?
How do you clean up so you do not bring silica dust home to your family?
